items.text: "If all the world were a golden ring,
Hormuz would be the jewel in it."

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So where exactly is the Strait of Hormuz?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Right here. Between Iran and Oman, at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And why is everyone talking about it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Oil. Almost every tanker leaving the Gulf has to pass through here. That's about one barrel in every five the world uses.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Wow. How wide is it?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About twenty-one miles at its narrowest. And the shipping lanes? Just two miles wide each way.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Was it always this important?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Long before oil. Back in 1272, Marco Polo passed through and saw ships from India unloading spices, pearls and silk.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Wait, the city was on the mainland back then?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Right. Then around 1300, to escape raiders, its rulers moved the whole city onto a bare island offshore.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A century later, Chinese treasure fleets anchored there too.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Sounds like a pretty rich place.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: It was. People said: if all the world were a golden ring, Hormuz would be the jewel in it.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Let me guess. Someone wanted that jewel.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Right. In 1507, the Portuguese commander Afonso de Albuquerque arrived, burned the harbour's ships and forced the king to pay tribute.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: But here's the thing: three of his own captains sailed off, and he had to leave.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So he gave up?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Not exactly. He came back in 1515 with twenty-seven ships, and Hormuz gave in.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: For about a century, ships between India, Persia and Arabia had to deal with Portuguese Hormuz.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And nobody pushed back?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Persia's Shah Abbas did. He wanted it back. He had a great army. But he didn't have a navy.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Wait, so what happened next?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: That's Part 2. Like the video and follow History Sketches so you don't miss it. And tell us in the comments what you think!
